arguments.summary: Company contribution: conditional earnings sensitivities are available for NVDA and MU, anchored to reported US-GAAP interim EPS and management outlooks. NVDA’s grid has bull upside larger than bear loss; MU’s is essentially symmetric with slightly greater bear loss. QQQ provides dated, diversified but meaningful look-through exposure to both issuers; its sponsor aggregate P/E is not methodologically interchangeable with the companies’ assumed P/E stresses.

claims.text: NVDA reported $4.85 of US-GAAP diluted EPS for the first six months of FY2027; FY2027 is a 53-week year ending January 31, 2027, with a 14-week fourth quarter. Q2 revenue was $96.2bn and Data Center revenue $89.0bn; Q3 outlook calls for $108.0bn revenue plus/minus 2%, 74.0% GAAP gross margin, about $9.2bn GAAP opex, and assumes no China Data Center compute revenue. These are the operating anchors, not a Q4 forecast.

NVDA’s explicitly hypothetical FY2027 US-GAAP EPS/P-E grid is $8/20x, $10/24x and $12/28x. The respective constant-share residuals after reported first-half EPS are $3.15/$5.15/$7.15; they are approximations because future diluted shares are unknown. The base requires $5.15 in H2, with Q3 guidance supporting only part of that bridge and no Q4 guidance supplied. At the dated close, base break-even is 22.227x holding $10 EPS fixed, or $9.26125 holding 24x fixed: either threshold only equates value to the close, and a higher EPS or multiple is needed for upside. Bear/base/bull sensitivities are -28.02%/+7.98%/+51.17%; bull upside exceeds absolute bear loss by 23.15 percentage points, a mechanical asymmetry without probability or fair-value implication. Demand durability through the Q3 ramp and longer Q4 supports the base/bull mechanisms; a Q3 miss, weaker margin, or inability to sustain the ramp supports the bear mechanism.

MU reported $41.40 of US-GAAP diluted EPS for the first nine months of FY2026. Its 53-week FY2026 ends September 3, 2026 and includes a 14-week Q4; the year had ended by the research cutoff but results were scheduled for September 30, so annual EPS remains a provisional historical estimate rather than future growth. Q3 revenue was $41.456bn and GAAP EPS $24.67. Q4 GAAP guidance was $30.73 plus/minus $1.00, with $50.0bn plus/minus $1.0bn revenue and about 86% gross margin. Management identified high-volume HBM4 shipments and AI-memory demand as drivers.

MU’s hypothetical FY2026 US-GAAP EPS/P-E grid is $70/11x, $72.13/14x and $74/17x. The implied Q4 constant-share residuals are $28.60/$30.73/$32.60: bear is below the $29.73-$31.73 GAAP guidance interval, base equals its midpoint, and bull is above it. They test demand/pricing/mix and margin execution around the AI-memory ramp, not consensus. At the dated close, base break-even is 14.0829058644x holding $72.13 EPS fixed, or $72.5571428571 holding 14x fixed; exceeding—not merely reaching—one threshold while the other is fixed is required for upside. Bear/base/bull sensitivities are -24.20%/-0.59%/+23.84%; bear loss exceeds bull gain by only 0.35 percentage points, near symmetry rather than a meaningful skew. The September 30 release is the immediate observable test of the residual and margin assumptions.

QQQ’s dated September 18 sponsor holdings assign 8.535228% to NVDA and 5.012336% to MU, within reported equity-weight coverage of 99.859505%. QQQ’s sponsor-reported aggregate P/E was 30.08 as of August 31. Thus QQQ has material dated look-through exposure to both issuers but also diversification beyond them; its aggregate fund P/E cannot be directly compared to hypothetical single-company annual EPS/P-E stresses or used to infer either company’s observed multiple.

Within the supplied conditional grids, NVDA requires a less complete second-half bridge because only Q3 is guided, whereas MU’s base residual exactly matches Q4 GAAP midpoint guidance. MU nevertheless has a completed fiscal year awaiting results and a more cycle-sensitive demand/pricing/margin stress in the bear case; NVDA’s main modeled challenge is sustaining its Data Center ramp into an unguided Q4. This is a comparison of disclosed anchors and stated scenarios, not a cross-company ranking, probability estimate, or claim that either P/E band is fair.

gaps.description: No forward diluted-share counts are supplied. Residual EPS bridges in both grids use a constant-share approximation and cannot reconcile reported interim EPS to final annual diluted EPS exactly.

No consensus estimates, observed company P/E multiples, or empirical multiple histories are supplied. The grids support only explicitly hypothetical sensitivity analysis, not a fair-value, normal-multiple, or unconditional relative-valuation conclusion.

QQQ’s aggregate P/E is dated August 31 while holdings are dated September 18, and sponsor fund methodology is not equivalent to company EPS/P-E sensitivity. It supports dated overlap, not a synthetic issuer-level valuation comparison.

assumptions: All grid EPS and P/E values are analyst stress assumptions rather than consensus, observed multiples, targets, probabilities, or fair-value estimates.
The annual earnings periods differ from the 63-session horizon: NVDA FY2027 ends January 31, 2027; MU FY2026 ended September 3, 2026 and awaited its September 30 release.
Residual EPS is annual assumed EPS less reported interim EPS using a constant diluted-share approximation only.
QQQ holdings and valuation are dated sponsor observations, not current holdings or a personalized portfolio exposure.
arguments.counter_thesis: NVDA’s demand ramp could hold despite no Q4 guidance and MU could report above guided Q4 EPS; conversely, valuation compression can dominate even if either issuer meets its earnings bridge. The evidence does not empirically weight those alternatives.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA’s next reported quarter against the $108.0bn plus/minus 2% revenue, 74.0% GAAP gross-margin and roughly $9.2bn GAAP-opex anchors; a revenue/margin shortfall weakens the $5.15 base H2 residual, while execution consistent with those anchors supports retaining it pending Q4 evidence.

Review MU’s September 30 FY2026 results against the $30.73 plus/minus $1.00 GAAP Q4 EPS interval and approximately 86% gross-margin guidance; a result below the interval validates the bear residual mechanism, while a result above it validates the bull mechanism and replaces the provisional annual estimate.

shared_exposures.mechanism: QQQ’s September 18 holdings include NVDA and MU at 8.535228% and 5.012336%, respectively, so issuer-specific earnings/demand surprises can transmit to the fund alongside numerous other constituents. Reported equity coverage is 99.859505%; this is dated fund composition, not an investor allocation or a claim of current weights.
shared_exposures.qualification: The direction and magnitude of fund transmission depend on other holdings, index movements, and later rebalancing; the sponsor aggregate P/E is not a company multiple.
